summary: A round stone tower lit in 1843 on a bare islet in the St. Lawrence off Saint-Jean-Port-Joli, kept by local families until 1960.

notes_for_editor: Keeper roster and the 1857 Canadian wreck rest on Lighthouse Friends alone (one Leclerc appointment date cross-checked in a Marine report). Builder named Joseph Andrew (Quebec register) vs Joseph Archer (Lighthouse Friends). Tower height 15.9 m vs 18.3 m; a Parks Canada passage prints 1834 for 1843. Fire date: Lighthouse Friends says July 1913, Quebec register says new lantern/house 1914, the Marine report listing the replacement works is for FY ended 31 Mar 1915; the report's amounts were matched to Stone Pillar by position in OCR'd table columns (4,444.44 and 3,383.21 agree with Lighthouse Friends). Dates of Henry B. Hall (10 June 1915) and Canadian Recruit (18 Aug 1921) are inferred from the fiscal year of the report volume. Canada Parks DFHD pages are JS-rendered, so the Parks Canada text is read through heritageguide.ca. No newspapers searched. The Placoteux article mentions a heliport; public access unclear. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the Geo. Leclerc line (source 6) was read on the page image; it sits under 'Algernon Rock' (salary 700), not 'Stone Pillar', since the Department combined the two posts. Lighthouse Friends dates Roche's petition 1860 but its quoted vote 1859, and the vote names L'Islet; the Placoteux article places the Canadian near the roche à Veillon, not Algernon Rock. The Coast Guard list of lights gives 12.7 m beside the tower description, a third height. The Quebec register's sector page spells the last keeper Antoine Bourgault. The federal designation is Canadian Register record 20716 (not 14775).
